questions.qtext:
Consider the following C code:

typedef struct { int x, y; } Point;
typedef struct { Point* p; } Box;
int rotate(int a, Box* b) {
 int t = a;
 a = b->p->x;
 b->p->x = b->p->y;
 b->p->y = t;
 return a;
}
int main() {
 int a = 3;
 Point* p = malloc(sizeof(Point));
 p->x = 10; p->y = 5;
 Box b1 = {p};
 a = rotate(a, &b1);
 printf("%d\n", a);
 free(p);
 return 0;
}


What is the value printed by printf?

questions.qtext:
Consider the following C function: 

bool findSomething(int a[], int b[], int length) {
 for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
 bool found = false;
 for (int j = 0; j < length; j++) {
 if (a[i] == b[j]) {
 found = true;
 break;
 }
 }
 if (!found)
 return false;
 }
 return true;
}


Precondition: Arrays $a$ and $b$ have equal length.

Which best describes what the function findSomething does? It returns true only if:

options.text: Arrays $a$ and $b$ contain identical elements in the same order.
Arrays $a$ and $b$ contain identical elements in reverse order.
Arrays $a$ and $b$ are permutations of each other.
Every element of array $a$ is also in $b$, and every element of array $b$ is also in $a$
